candidates.name: Glioma
support_spans: Vitreous biopsy: Hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm, small to medium-sized cells with scant cytoplasm and oval, pleomorphic, hyperchromatic nuclei
Immunohistochemistry: Positive for glial fibrillary acid protein, oligodendrocyte transcription factor 2, mutant IDH-1 protein, p53; Loss of ATRX protein; Ki-67 proliferation index ~10%
candidates.why: The presence of astrocytic neoplasm and specific immunohistochemical markers supports the diagnosis of glioma.

candidates.name: Optic Neuritis
support_spans: Right eye showed full visual field, right-sided relative afferent pupillary defect, unremarkable anterior segment, and mild swelling of the optic disc
candidates.why: The initial presentation of mild swelling of the optic disc and relative afferent pupillary defect suggests optic neuritis.

candidates.name: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
support_spans: Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein
candidates.why: The finding of combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein supports this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Glioma
support_spans: Vitreous biopsy: Hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm, small to medium-sized cells with scant cytoplasm and oval, pleomorphic, hyperchromatic nuclei
Immunohistochemistry: Positive for glial fibrillary acid protein, oligodendrocyte transcription factor 2, mutant IDH-1 protein, p53; Loss of ATRX protein; Ki-67 proliferation index ~10%
candidates.why: The patient's vitreous biopsy and immunohistochemistry results are consistent with a glioma, specifically an astrocytic neoplasm.

candidates.name: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
support_spans: Follow-up examination (after vision loss): Right eye showed no light perception vision, marked swelling of the optic disc, peripapillary retinal hemorrhages, and occlusion of the superior branch artery.
Wide-field fluorescein angiography: Showed choroidal flush but complete lack of perfusion of retinal vasculature
candidates.why: The patient's sudden vision loss and lack of perfusion of retinal vasculature are consistent with a central retinal artery occlusion.

candidates.name: Optic Neuritis
support_spans: Right eye showed full visual field, right-sided relative afferent pupillary defect, unremarkable anterior segment, and mild swelling of the optic disc.
Coronal T1-weighted contrast-enhanced image: Focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve
candidates.why: The patient's initial presentation with mild swelling of the optic disc and relative afferent pupillary defect is consistent with optic neuritis.

selector.rationale: Vitreous biopsy showing astrocytic neoplasm and immunohistochemistry results support glioma, with glioblastoma being a subtype but less specifically supported by the evidence

rejected.label: Optic Neuritis
rejected.why: Mild swelling of the optic disc and relative afferent pupillary defect are not sufficient to explain the sudden vision loss and other findings

rejected.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
rejected.why: While occlusion is present, it does not account for the astrocytic neoplasm found in the vitreous biopsy
